caption: The drawing depicts a single object, a powder horn, shown against a plain, light beige background. The powder horn is rendered in realistic tones, with the thicker end primarily a light ivory color and the narrower tip a gradient of light to medium brown. Decorative, scalloped engravings are visible near the wider end, where the color transitions from brown to ivory. The main part of the horn features inscribed calligraphy in a dark brown color with the text "James Shan Men May 26 1788." At the lower left corner of the drawing, a small inset sketch outlines the shape of the horn and indicates its length as "11"" (11 inches), with a simple line and number. The outer edges of the drawing are bordered by a thin, red rectangular line, and at the bottom right, handwritten text reads "DEL. 156-1 James M. Lawson." The composition is centered, placing the powder horn as the main focus of the artwork.
title: Powder Horn
